statement: Stack 1 is 1 can. Stack 2 has rows of 2 and 1 cans. Stack 3 has rows of 3, 2 and 1 cans, and so on. How many cans are in stack 5?

choices.misconception: I only counted the bottom row of stack 5.
I worked out stack 4 instead of stack 5.
I put 6 cans in the bottom row, one more than the stack number.
I gave every row of stack 5 the same 5 cans.

hints: How many cans are in the bottom row of stack 5?
Each stack has a bottom row as long as the stack number, and each row above has one can fewer, up to 1 can at the top. Add the rows.
Stack 5 has rows of 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 cans. Add them.

solutions.reliable: Stack 5 has rows of 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 cans, so it has $5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15$ cans. Check with the pattern: stacks 1 to 4 have 1, 3, 6 and 10 cans, and each new stack adds a new bottom row one longer than before, so stack 5 adds 5 to make $10 + 5 = 15$. The idea to keep: see how each picture is built from the one before.
solutions.elegant: Pair the rows: $5 + 0$, $4 + 1$, $3 + 2$ each make 5, and there are 3 pairs, so 15. The idea to keep: pairing numbers to the same total makes adding quick.

whyOnTest: Growing patterns test whether a student sees what each new step adds, not just the last number.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
